nahhas-irab:1-1.t: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā said: everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is «يس»; whoever recites it by day is relieved of his worry, and whoever recites it by night has his sin forgiven. Shahr ibn Ḥawshab said: the people of Paradise will recite only «طه» and «يس». Abū Jaʿfar said: there are several readings of «يس». The people of Medina and al-Kisāʾī read (يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ) assimilating the nūn into the wāw; Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ) pronouncing the nūn distinctly; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «يسينَ والقرآن الحكيم»; and al-Farrāʾ mentioned a fourth reading, «ياسينِ والقرآن». [Translator's note: the source prints the variants without vowels; the endings shown follow the explanations that come after.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading, with assimilation, is as Arabic requires, because the nūn is assimilated into the wāw on account of its resemblance to it. Whoever pronounces it distinctly says: the way of the letters of the alphabet is to be paused upon, and assimilation is only in continuous speech. Sībawayh mentioned the accusative and gave it two explanations: one, that it is an object which he does not decline, because in his view it is a foreign name like «هابيل»; the implied form being "Mention Yāsīn"; and Sībawayh made it a name of the sūra. His other view is that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, like «كيف» and «أين». As for the kasra, al-Farrāʾ claimed it is likened to the Arabs' saying «جَيْرِ لأفعلنّ» and «جَيْرِ لا أفعل» ("indeed, I will do…", "indeed, I will not do…").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (وَسَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ): it was said: the meaning is that they do not care about that nor pay heed to it, and they do not believe. Ibn ʿAbbās said: not one of them believed.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (إِنَّما تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ), i.e. only he benefits from the warning. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of (وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ) is: he feared Allah, Mighty and Majestic, where no one sees him except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk reported from Ibn ʿAbbās on the meaning of «كريم»: i.e. good; and it was said: by it Paradise is meant; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: The original of (إِنَّا) is «إنّنا»; the nūn was dropped because of the coming together of the nūns. (نُحْيِ): the ḍamma was dropped from it because of its heaviness, and assimilating the yāʾ into the yāʾ is not permissible here, lest two quiescent letters meet. (وَنَكْتُبُ ما قَدَّمُوا وَآثارَهُمْ), i.e. the record of what they sent ahead; the muḍāf ilayhi was put in the place of the muḍāf. Ibn ʿAbbās interpreted it as their steps to the mosques, and this is the most fitting of what has been said about it, because he said the verse was revealed about that, since the homes of the Anṣār were far from the mosque. In the ḥadīth of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith from Abū ʿUshāna from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "For one foot a good deed is written for him, and for the other an evil deed is removed from him, going and returning, when he goes out to the mosque." Others than Ibn ʿAbbās interpreted «ونكتب ما قدّموا وآثارهم» to mean: We write the good they sent ahead and the good practice (sunna) they established which is acted upon after them. The singular of «الآثار» is «أَثَر», and one also says «إِثْر». (وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ) is accusative on the implication of a verb; its nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) is permissible, except that its accusative is preferable, so that what the verb governs is conjoined to what the verb governs. This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them. Mujāhid said: (فِي إِمامٍ مُبِينٍ) — in the Preserved Tablet.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحابَ الْقَرْيَةِ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. mention to them a parable. «الضَّرْب» is the likeness and the kind; one says «هذا من ضرب هذا», i.e. of the likeness and kind of this. The meaning is: and set forth for them a likeness. (أَصْحابَ الْقَرْيَةِ) is a badal (substitute) for «مثل», so the meaning is "the likeness of the people of the town". (إِذْ جاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ), i.e. the messengers came to its people.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (إِذْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُما فَعَزَّزْنا بِثالِثٍ): ʿĀṣim read «فعَزَزْنا» [without doubling]. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading as (فَعَزَّزْنا), the same as the standard text; the following discussion shows the variant without shadda.] Some people have perhaps erred in this, imagining that it is from «عزّ يعِزّ» (to be mighty); it is not from it, but from the Arabs' saying «عازّني فلان فعززته أعُزّه», i.e. I overcame and subdued him; and it has parallels in their speech. Al-Farrāʾ interpreted (فَعَزَّزْنا بِثالِثٍ) as meaning that the third was sent before the two, that he was Simʿān (Shamʿūn), and that the meaning of «فعززنا به» is that he overcame them. The apparent wording indicates the opposite of what he said; had it been as he said, it would have been more fitting in the speech of the Arabs to say «بالثالث» (with the third), since he had been sent before — as one says at the beginning of a letter «سلامٌ عليك» and at its end «والسلام», and as one says «مررتُ برجلٍ من قصّته كذا، فقلت للرجل».

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: (وَالْقُرْآنِ): an oath. The wāw is substituted for the bāʾ because of its resemblance to it, just as they substituted it for «ربّ». [Translator's note: the source reads «مبدلة من ياء», evidently for «من باء» "for the bāʾ".] (الْحَكِيمِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «القرآن». Abū Isḥāq said: because it is made firm (uḥkima) with command and prohibition, parables and the stories of the nations.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The answer to the oath. «إنّ» has kasra because there is the lām in its khabar (predicate); and were the lām omitted it would still have kasra, except in the view of al-Kisāʾī, for he permits its fatḥa, because there is in the statement the meaning of "I swear".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. on a straight way. Qatāda said: i.e. on a straight religion. Abū Isḥāq said: (عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar. He said: it may also be part of the ṣila (relative clause) of «المرسلين», i.e. those who were sent on a straight path.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: This [nominative] is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr; the Kufans and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Yaḥṣubī read (تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ) in the accusative, and the genitive has been reported. Abū Jaʿfar said: the nominative is on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "what has been sent down to you is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful"; the accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and the genitive is as a badal (substitute) for «القرآن».

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْماً ما أُنْذِرَ آباؤُهُمْ): «ما» has no grammatical position according to most of the people of tafsīr, because it is negative. According to the view of ʿIkrima its position is accusative, because he said: i.e. their fathers had been warned; on this basis it is like His words (فَقُلْ أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ صاعِقَةً) [Fuṣṣilat: 13], i.e. of a thunderbolt. (فَهُمْ غافِلُونَ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلى أَكْثَرِهِمْ), i.e. the word of punishment has come true against them because of their disbelief; and like it is (وَلكِنْ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذابِ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ) [al-Zumar: 71].

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (إِنَّا جَعَلْنا فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلالًا): from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Abū Jahl swore, "If I see Muḥammad ﷺ praying, I will smash his head." So he took a stone, while the Prophet ﷺ was praying, to throw it at him; and when he raised it towards him, his hand dried up against his neck and the stone stuck to his hand. On this basis it is a figurative comparison, i.e. like one whose hand is shackled to his neck. Ibn ʿUyayna reported from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār; he said: Ibn ʿAbbās read «إنّا جعلنا في أيمانهم أغلالاً فهي إلى الأذقان». Abū Isḥāq said: and it was read «إنّا جعلنا في أيديهم أغلالاً». Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is by way of explanation, and one does not recite what differs from the muṣḥaf. In the statement, according to the reading of the majority, there is an omission; the implied form is "We have put on their necks and on their hands shackles, and they are up to the chins", so «هي» refers to the hands, not to the necks. The Arabs omit the like of this; its parallel is (سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ) [al-Naḥl: 81], whose implied form is "and garments which protect you from the cold", omitted because what protects from heat protects from cold; and because when the shackle is on the neck, it must also be on the hand — especially since He, Mighty and Majestic, said (فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقانِ), so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made known that by it the hands are meant. (فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ): the most important of what has been reported about it is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā related: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, showed them «الإقماح»: he put his hands under his beard, joined them, and raised his head. Abū Jaʿfar said: this was taken from what al-Aṣmaʿī related; he said: one says «أكمحتُ الدابّة» when you pull its bridle so that it raises its head. [Translator's note: the source reads «لترف رأسها», evidently for «لترفع رأسها».] Abū Jaʿfar said: the qāf is substituted for the kāf because of its closeness to it, as one says «قهرته» and «كهرته». Al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says «أكفحتُ الدابّة» when you meet its mouth with the bridle to strike it with it; derived from their saying «لقيته كفاحاً», i.e. face to face. And «كفحتُ الدابّة», without alif, when you pull its reins so that it stops and does not run.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said in his narration: ʿUtba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl and Umayya ibn Khalaf sat lying in wait for the Prophet ﷺ to inflict harm on him. He came out to them reciting the beginning of «يس», with dust in his hand, and threw it at them, and recited (وَجَعَلْنا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا) up to the end of the tenth [verse]; and they lowered their heads until the Prophet ﷺ had passed. And it has been said that this is a figurative comparison, as one says "So-and-so is a donkey", i.e. he does not see guidance, as is said: [al-Basīṭ] 359-
لهم عن الرشد أغلال وأقياد
(They have, [keeping them] from right guidance, shackles and fetters.)
The reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz is «فأعشيناهم» [with ʿayn]. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading as (فَأَغْشَيْناهُمْ), the same as the standard text; the following discussion shows the variant is with ʿayn.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading with ghayn fits the flow of the speech better; one says «غشيه الأمر» and «أغشيته إيّاه». As for «فأعشيناهم», it is said only of one whose sight has become weak so that he cannot see at night, or of one who acts as he does, as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 360-
متى تأته تعشو إلى ضوء ناره ... تجد خير نار عندها خير موقد
(Whenever you come to him, making your dim-sighted way to the light of his fire, you find the best of fires with the best of kindlers beside it.)
Qatāda said: (فَهُمْ لا يُبْصِرُونَ) guidance.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (قالُوا ما أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا): mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: (لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ), i.e. we will surely kill you. He said: most of what is in the Qurʾān of «الرجم» (stoning) means killing.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (قالُوا طائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَإِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ): there are seven readings in it. The people of Medina read «أين ذكّرتم» [i.e. «أَيِن»], lightening the second hamza; the people of Kufa read (أَإِنْ) pronouncing both hamzas fully; the third way is «أاإن», with two hamzas and an alif between them, the alif being inserted out of dislike of combining two hamzas; the fourth way is «أاإن» with a hamza, after it an alif, and after the alif a lightened hamza; the fifth reading is «أان ذكّرتم» with two hamzas, except that the second is a lightened hamza; and the sixth way is «أأن» with two fully pronounced hamzas, both with fatḥa — al-Farrāʾ reported that this is the reading of Abū Razīn. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «قالوا طائركم معكم أَيْنَ ذُكِّرتم», with «أين» in the sense of «حيث» (wherever); the meaning is "wherever you are reminded, your ill omen is with you". The meaning of «أأن» is «ألأن» ("is it because…?"). Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa read «ذُكِرتم» without doubling. [Translator's note: the source counts seven readings but explicitly numbers six; the reading with «أين» is presumably the seventh. The vowelling of the variants is not marked in the source and is supplied from the descriptions.] Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning of (طائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ) is: your provision and your deeds. (بَلْ) is for moving from one statement to another. (أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: (وَجاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعى), and in another place (رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعى) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 20]; the meaning is the same, except that the proper place of adverbial expressions is at the end of the statement, and putting them first is a licence (majāz). Do you not see that the meaning of «إنّ في الدار زيداً» is «إنّ زيداً في الدار»? (قالَ يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوا الْمُرْسَلِينَ).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: (اتَّبِعُوا مَنْ لا يَسْئَلُكُمْ أَجْراً): this indicates the repetition of the verb. (وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) is construed according to the meaning of «مَن».

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «وما لِيْ لا أعبد» with the yāʾ quiescent. [Translator's note: the source prints the reading with the standard vowelling, (وَما لِيَ لا أَعْبُدُ).] This is the yāʾ of the first person, which takes fatḥa or is made quiescent when what precedes it is vowelled: fatḥa because it is a noun, and it is disliked that a noun consisting of one letter be quiescent; and quiescence because of its being attached to what precedes it. The position of (لا أَعْبُدُ) is the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمنُ بِضُرٍّ): a condition and its apodosis. The sign of the jussive in it is the dropping of the ḍamma from the dāl, and the yāʾ before the dāl was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. What is said about the yāʾ after the nūn is as has preceded, regarding fatḥa and quiescence, except that if you make it quiescent you drop it in continuous speech because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (لا تُغْنِ عَنِّي).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: As for what is reported from ʿĀṣim, that he read (إِنِّي آمَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ) with fatḥa on the nūn [«فاسمعونَ»], it is a solecism (laḥn), because it is in the position of the jussive [imperative]; if you put kasra on the nūn it is permissible, because it is the nūn that accompanies the yāʾ, not the nūn of iʿrāb. Abū Isḥāq said: he called the messengers to witness his faith, and said: (إِنِّي آمَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ).

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قالَ يا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (26)

(قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ): there is an omission in the statement because the hearer knows it. The implied form is: "So they killed him, and it was said: Enter Paradise; and when he saw the bliss he was in, (قالَ يا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ)."

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (بِما غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي): there are three ways in it: «ما» may be maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun), it may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which), and the third is interrogative; this last is weak, because what is most frequent in the interrogative is «بِمَ غفر لي ربّي؟» without alif. (وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ): Abū Mijlaz said: i.e. because of my faith and my believing the messengers. Abū Isḥāq said: (مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ), i.e. He admitted me to Paradise.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (وَما أَنْزَلْنا عَلى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ), i.e. He did not send down an army from the sky to avenge him.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (إِنْ كانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً): in «كانت» there is an implied [subject], i.e. their punishment, or their affliction, was nothing but a single cry. Abū Jaʿfar [Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ] read «إن كانت إلّا صيحةٌ واحدةٌ» in the nominative. Abū Ḥātim said: this ought not to be permissible, because one says only «ما جاءني إلّا جاريتُك» ("none came to me but your slave-girl"), and one does not say «ما جاءتني إلّا جاريتك», because the meaning is "no one came to me except your slave-girl"; so had it been as Abū Jaʿfar read, he would have said «إن كان إلّا صيحةٌ واحدة». Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: nothing prevents this; one says «ما جاءتني إلّا جاريتك», meaning "no woman, or no slave-girl, came to me". The implied form of the nominative in the reading is what Abū Isḥāq said; he said: the meaning is "there was not against them a cry except a single cry". Others construed it as meaning "nothing occurred except a single cry", and «كان» in the sense of "occurred" is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad read — and it is said that it is so in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] — «إن كانت إلّا زقيةً واحدة». Abū Jaʿfar said: this differs from the muṣḥaf; moreover, the known usage is «زقا يزقو» when it cries out, so on this basis it should have been «إلّا زقوة». Qatāda said: (فَإِذا هُمْ خامِدُونَ), i.e. perished.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
(يا حَسْرَةً) is accusative because it is the vocative of an indefinite noun, in which only the accusative is permissible according to the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the accusative is the preferred choice, and that were the indefinite noun connected to a qualifier put in the nominative, it would be correct; he cited as evidence several things, among them that he heard from the Arabs «يا مهتمٌّ بأمرنا لا تهتمّ» ("O one concerned about our affair, do not be concerned"). [Translator's note: the source first writes «يا مهمّ», then «يا مهتمّ»; the latter is meant.] And he recited: [al-Kāmil] 361-
يا دار غيّرها البلى تغييرا
(O abode which decay has thoroughly changed.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: in this is the invalidation of the chapter of the vocative, or most of it, because he puts in the nominative the purely indefinite noun, puts in the nominative what is like a muḍāf in its length, drops the tanwīn in mid-position, and puts in the nominative what is in meaning an object, without any cause requiring that. As for what he related from the Arabs, it does not resemble what he permitted, because the implied form of «يا مهتمّ بأمرنا لا تهتمّ» is by way of fronting and postponement, the meaning being "O you who are concerned, do not be concerned about our affair". And the implied form of the verse of poetry is "O you abode", and then he turned the address, i.e. "O people, decay has changed this abode", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (حَتَّى إِذا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ) [Yūnus: 22]. Abū Isḥāq used to say that His words, Mighty and Majestic, (يا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبادِ) are among the most difficult questions in the Qurʾān. He said this only because the question about it is: what is the benefit of calling upon regret? Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh explained this in the best way. His position is that when «يا عجباه» is said, its meaning is "O wonder, this is your time and one of your times at which you ought to be present". [Translator's note: the source reads «من أبانك», evidently for «من إبّانك» "your time".] The meaning according to his view is that regret ought to be present for them over themselves because of their mockery of the messengers. On the meaning of the verse there is an unusual view with a good chain of transmission, reported by al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas from Abū al-ʿĀliya; he said: when the disbelievers saw the punishment, they said "Alas for the servants!", meaning by "the servants" the three messengers who were sent to them; they grieved over having lost them, since they had not been present so that they might believe. Allah the Exalted said: (ما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) [al-Ḥijr: 11].

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ): al-Farrāʾ said: «كم» is in the position of the accusative in two ways: one is by «يروا», and he cited as evidence for this view that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is «ألم يروا مَن أهلكنا»; the other way is that «كم» is in the position of the accusative by «أهلكنا». Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is impossible, because «كم» cannot be governed by what precedes it, since it is interrogative, and it is impossible for an interrogative to enter the domain of what precedes it; and likewise is its rule when it is declarative. Sībawayh did hint at some of this, making «أنّهم» a badal (substitute) for «كم», and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd refuted him for this in the strongest terms, and said: «كم» is in the position of the accusative by «أهلكنا», and «أنّهم» is in the position of the accusative; the meaning according to him is «بأنّهم», i.e. "Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them by extermination?"

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: This is «إنّ», heavy in origin, lightened, so that it lost its governing in most dialects, and the lām became necessary with it to distinguish it from the «إن» which is in the sense of «ما» (not). The Kufans read (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا), and there are two views on it. One is that «لمّا» is in the sense of «إلّا» (except) and «إن» in the sense of «ما»; Sībawayh reported that in their saying «سألتك بالله لمّا فعلت» ("I ask you by Allah, [do nothing] but do it"); and al-Kisāʾī claimed that he does not know this. The other view is that the meaning is «وإن كلٌّ لَمِن ما», and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. He said: and [one of the] «ما» was dropped, as one says «علماءِ بنو فلان», meaning by it «على الماءِ بنو فلان» ("the Banū so-and-so are at the water").

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (وَآيَةٌ) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «لَهُمُ»; the khabar may also be (الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ). Abū Isḥāq said: one also says «الميّتة», and the light form is more frequent.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَما عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ): «ما» is in the position of the genitive by conjunction, i.e. "and of what their hands made". «ما» may also be negative with no position, i.e. "and their hands did not make it". When it is with the hāʾ dropped [«وما عملت أيديهم»], «ما» is in the position of the genitive, the hāʾ being dropped because of the length of the noun; and it is unlikely then that it is negative.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. the kinds of animals and plants.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ): and a sign indicating the oneness of Allah.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي): its implied form may be "and a sign for them is the sun"; «الشمس» may be nominative by an implied verb which the second explains; and it may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
﴿وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ حَتَّى عادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ﴾ (39)

(وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ): its implied form [in the nominative reading] may be "and a sign for them is the moon"; and «القمر» may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). The Kufans read (وَالْقَمَرَ) in the accusative on the implication of a verb, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: because before it there is a verb and after it a verb like it: before it «نسلخ» and after it «قدّرناه». Abū Jaʿfar said: the people of Arabic, all of them as far as I know, are against what he said, among them al-Farrāʾ, who said: the nominative is more pleasing to me. The nominative was preferable in the view of both of them only because it is conjoined to what precedes it, so its meaning is "and a sign is the moon". As for his saying that «نسلخ» precedes it — there is before it something nearer to it than that, namely «يجري», and before that «والشمس» in the nominative; and what he mentioned after it, «قدّرناه», has already governed the hāʾ. A second way in the nominative: it is nominative as mubtadaʾ. And it may be said: the moon is not the stations, so how did He say "We determined it stations"? There are two answers to this. One is that its implied form is "We determined it as possessing stations", like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. The other implied form is "We determined for it stations", then the lām was omitted; its omission was good because the verb is transitive to two objects, like (وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا) [al-Aʿrāf: 155].

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: You made «الشمس» nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); «لا» may not govern a definite noun. The scholars have spoken about the meaning of this verse. Some of them said its meaning is that the sun does not overtake the moon so as to cancel its meaning [i.e. its light]. It was said: the moon is in the lowest heaven and the sun in the fourth heaven, so it does not overtake it. The best and clearest of what has been said about its meaning, which cannot be rejected, is that the course of the moon is a fast course, so the sun does not overtake it in its course. (وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ) is also among what they have discussed. Some of them said: this indicates that the day was created before the night, and that the night did not precede it in creation. It was said: neither of them can precede the other, because the existence of this one is the non-existence of that one, and before and after do not apply to them; this is the view of the people of reasoning. It was said: each of them comes in its time, neither preceding the other. Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd and ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; he said: I heard ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl ibn Jarīr recite «ولا الليلُ سابقُ النهارَ». I said: "What is this?" He said: "I meant «سابقٌ النهارَ», and I dropped the tanwīn because it is lighter." [Translator's note: the source prints the recitation with the standard vowelling (وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ); the accusative «النهارَ» is required by the explanation.] Abū Jaʿfar said: «النهار» may be accusative, without tanwīn [on «سابق»], the tanwīn having been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: This verse is among the most difficult in the sūra, because of His words, Mighty and Majestic, (حَمَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ), since it is they who are carried. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the two pronouns are different, and the meaning is: "And a sign for the people of Mecca is that We carried the offspring of the people of Nūḥ in the ship." There is another good view on it: that the meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed of His kindness and favour that He created ships in which are carried those for whom walking and riding are difficult, of the offspring and the little ones; on this basis the two pronouns agree.

nahhas-irab:42-43.t: (وَخَلَقْنا لَهُمْ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ ما يَرْكَبُونَ): the original is «يركبونه»; the hāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun, and because it is the end of a verse. There are three views on its meaning. The position of Mujāhid, Qatāda and a group of the people of tafsīr is that «من مثله» refers to camels. The second view is that it refers to camels, beasts and everything that is ridden. The third view is that it refers to ships, and this is the soundest of them, because it has a connected chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās, reported by Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās: (وَخَلَقْنا لَهُمْ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ ما يَرْكَبُونَ) — he said: He created for them ships like it in which they ride. And by another chain, Ibn ʿAbbās argued that this is not about camels because after it comes (وَإِنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ). And it [i.e. «فلا صريخَ لهم»] is good, because after it comes something in which only the nominative is permissible, since it is definite, namely (وَلا هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ); and the grammarians prefer «لا رجلَ في الدار ولا زيدٌ». [Translator's note: the passage passes abruptly from the exegesis to the grammatical point about «لا» with an indefinite noun followed by a definite one; the bracketed reference is supplied.]

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنَّا): al-Kisāʾī said: it is accusative as an exception. Abū Isḥāq said: it is accusative because it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), i.e. for the sake of mercy. (وَمَتاعاً) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it. Qatāda said: (إِلى حِينٍ), i.e. until death.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: In His words, Mighty and Majestic, (ما يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ) there are five readings. Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read «وهم يَخَصِّمون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the khāʾ and shadda on the ṣād, and so Warsh reported from Nāfiʿ. As for the authorities on the readings and the companions of Nāfiʿ other than Warsh, they reported from him «وهم يَخْصِّمون» with the khāʾ quiescent and the ṣād doubled, combining two quiescent letters. ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read (وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ) with kasra on the khāʾ and the ṣād doubled. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «وهم يَخْصِمون» with the khāʾ quiescent and the ṣād single. And in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: «وهم يختصمون». [Translator's note: the source prints the variants without vowels; they are vowelled here according to the descriptions.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading, «وهم يَخَصِّمون», is the clearest of them. The original is «يختصمون»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, and its vowel was transferred to the hāʾ. [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for "the khāʾ".] Making the khāʾ quiescent is not permissible, because it combines two quiescent letters, neither of which is a letter of prolongation and softness; in the like of this only the concealment (ikhfāʾ) of the vowel is permissible, and it was not accurately recorded — just as (فَتُوبُوا إِلى بارِئِكُمْ) [al-Baqara: 54] was not accurately recorded from Abū ʿAmr except in the report of one who records the language accurately, as Sībawayh reported from him that he used to snatch the vowel (ikhtilās). As for «يَخِصِّمون», its original is also «يختصمون»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, then the khāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that this reading is better and more frequent; so he abandoned what is more fitting — casting the vowel of the tāʾ onto the khāʾ — and fetched another vowel for it, and combined a yāʾ and a kasra; and he claimed it is better and more frequent — yet how can it be more frequent, when the fatḥa is the reading of the people of Mecca, the people of Basra and the people of Medina? ʿIkrima said about His words, Mighty and Majestic, (إِنْ كانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً) [Yā Sīn: 29]: it is the first blowing of the Trumpet.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً): al-Aʿmash reported from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Abū Hurayra; he said: the Trumpet will be blown while people are in their markets — one bringing a milch-camel, one measuring cloth by the cubit, one passing by on some errand — (فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً وَلا إِلى أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ). Al-Farrāʾ mentioned two views on it: one, they will not return a word to their families; and the other, they will not return from their markets to their families.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
(وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ): there are two views on its meaning. Qatāda said: «الصُّوَر» is the plural of «صورة» (form), i.e. the spirits were blown into the forms; «صورة» and «صُوَر» are like «سورة» of a building and «سُوَر». Al-ʿAjjāj said: [al-Rajaz] 362-
فربّ ذي سرادق محجور ... سرت إليه في أعالي السّور
(Many a man with a guarded pavilion have I journeyed to, through the highest courses [of rank].)
It has been reported from Ibn Hurmuz that he read «ونفخ في الصُّوَر» [with fatḥa on the wāw], and in this there is no difficulty. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ); the variant is evidently «الصُّوَر».] As for «الصُّور» with the wāw quiescent, the correct view is that it is the horn; the ḥadīth and authoritative instruction from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came with that, and it is well known in the speech of the Arabs. The lexicographers recited: [al-Rajaz] 363-
نحن نطحناهم غداة الغورين ... بالضّابخات في غبار النقعين
نطحا شديدا لا كنطح الصّورين
(We butted them on the morning of the two Ghawrs, with [steeds] … in the dust of the two battlefields — a fierce butting, not like the butting of two horns.)

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا) is accusative as a vocative in genitive construct, i.e. "this is one of your days and your time" [i.e. "O our woe, this is your time"]. It may also be accusative in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), with the one addressed omitted; whereas the Kufans construe it as «وَيْ لنا», separated. When it is said to them: "Then why did you say «وَيْلَ زيدٍ», putting fatḥa on the lām, when it is a lām of the genitive? And why did you say «وَيْلٌ له», putting ḍamma on the lām and tanwīn? And then you reported «وَيْلُ زيدٍ» with ḍamma without tanwīn?" — they give reasons which are not sound. Abū Jaʿfar said: we will mention them, if Allah wills, in what follows. (مَنْ بَعَثَنا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنا): it may be asked: how did they say this, when according to your view they are among those punished in their graves? The answer is that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: they slept a sleep. Abū Ṣāliḥ said: when the first blowing is blown, the punishment is lifted from the people of the graves, and they sleep a sleep until the second blowing, and between the two are forty years; that is their saying (مَنْ بَعَثَنا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنا). Mujāhid said: i.e. the believers will say to them (هذا ما وَعَدَ الرَّحْمنُ). Qatāda said: those whom Allah guided said to them (هذا ما وَعَدَ الرَّحْمنُ). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. the angels said to them (هذا ما وَعَدَ الرَّحْمنُ). Abū Jaʿfar said: these views agree, because the angels are among the believers and among those whom Allah has guided. Mujāhid read — and it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās — «يا ويلنا مِن بَعْثِنا» ("Woe to us, for our being raised!"). [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (يا وَيْلَنا مَنْ بَعَثَنا); the known variant is «مِن بَعْثِنا».] Abū Jaʿfar said: on this [view — that the angels are counted among the believers] is interpreted the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ) [al-Bayyina: 7], and likewise the ḥadīth, "The believer is, with Allah, better than everything He created." [Translator's note: in the source this sentence follows the report of Mujāhid's reading; the bracketed link to the preceding remark about the angels is added.] It may be that the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, and other believers said «هذا ما وعد الرحمن»; the complete stop on this basis is «من مرقدنا», and «هذا» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «ما وعد الرحمن». «هذا» may also be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «مرقدنا», so that the complete stop is «من مرقدنا هذا», and «ما وعد الرحمن» is in the position of the nominative from three angles, of which Abū Isḥāq mentioned two. He said: it may be on the implication of «هذا»; and the second, that it is in the sense of "what the Most Merciful promised is true". Abū Jaʿfar said: and the third, that it is in the sense of "your being raised is what the Most Merciful promised".

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (فَإِذا هُمْ جَمِيعٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); «جميع» is indefinite, and (مُحْضَرُونَ) is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās said: their occupation is deflowering virgins. Abū Qilāba said: while a man of the people of Paradise is with his wife, it is said to him, "Move on to your [other] wife," and he says, "I am busy with my wife"; and it is said to him, "Move on to your [other] wife as well." And it was said: the people of Paradise are occupied, with the pleasures and bliss they are in, from concern for the people of sin, their destination to the Fire and the painful punishment they are in, even if they are their relatives and their families. [Translator's note: the source reads «أقوياء» ("strong"), evidently for «أقرباءهم» ("their relatives").] The Kufans read (فِي شُغُلٍ) with ḍamma on the shīn and the ghayn; and from Mujāhid «في شُغْلٍ» [with the ghayn quiescent]; Abū Ḥātim reported that this is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, that he read it so. [Translator's note: the source prints Mujāhid's reading with the same vowelling as the first, (فِي شُغُلٍ); the variant is evidently «شُغْل».] These are dialectal forms with one meaning; and one also says «شَغْل» with fatḥa on the shīn and the ghayn quiescent. (فاكِهُونَ) is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». From Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, that he read «فاكهين», putting it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: Mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). «هم» may also be a tawkīd (emphasis), with (وَأَزْواجُهُمْ) conjoined to the latent pronoun, and (مُتَّكِؤُنَ) a naʿt (adjective) of His word «فاكهون».

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: The second dāl [in «يدّعون»] is substituted for a tāʾ, because it is «يفتعلون» from «دعاء».

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (سَلامٌ) is nominative as a badal (substitute) for «ما». [Translator's note: the source reads «مرفوع عن البدل», evidently for «على البدل».] «ما» may also be indefinite, with «سلام» a naʿt (adjective) of it, i.e. "and they will have whatever they ask for, granted in peace"; and «ما» may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with (سَلامٌ) a khabar (predicate) of it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is «سلاماً», which is then a maṣdar (verbal noun); or, if you wish, in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and they will have what they ask for, granted in peace". (قَوْلًا) is a maṣdar, i.e. "We say it as a word on the Day of Resurrection"; and its meaning may be "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said this as a word".

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ): one also says «أعهِد» with kasra on the hāʾ, which would be from «عهد يعهِد». Abū Isḥāq said: «عهد يعهِد» may be like «حسب يحسِب». (أَنْ لا تَعْبُدُوا الشَّيْطانَ): al-Kisāʾī said: «لا» is for prohibition.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
﴿وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ (61)

(وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي): whoever gives the nūn kasra does so according to the original rule; whoever gives it ḍamma [«وأنُ اعبدوني»] dislikes a kasra followed by a ḍamma.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جِبِلًّا): this is the reading of the people of Medina and the two ʿĀṣims. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and al-Naḍr ibn Anas read «ولقد أضلّ منكم جُبُلّاً» with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ and the lām doubled; Ibn Kathīr and the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «جُبُلاً» with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ and the lām single; Abū ʿAmr read «جُبْلاً» with ḍamma on the jīm, the bāʾ quiescent and the lām single; and Abū Yaḥyā and al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read «جِبْلاً» with kasra on the jīm, the bāʾ quiescent and the lām single. [Translator's note: the source prints all these readings with the same vowelling as the standard text, (جِبِلًّا); they are vowelled here according to the descriptions given.] Abū Jaʿfar said: these are five readings; the clearest of them is the first reading. The proof of that is that they agreed in reading (وَالْجِبِلَّةَ الْأَوَّلِينَ) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 184]; and «جُبُل» would be the plural of «جِبِلّة». The derivation of all of it is one: it is from «جبل الله الخلق», i.e. He created them. A sixth reading has been mentioned, namely «ولقد أضلّ منكم جِيلاً كثيراً» with yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints it as (جِبِلًّا كَثِيراً) "with yāʾ"; the reading meant is evidently «جِيلاً».] (أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْقِلُونَ), i.e. you did indeed use to reason; this is by way of rebuke; and likewise «ألم أعهد», i.e. I did indeed charge you.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: (وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَطَمَسْنا عَلى أَعْيُنِهِمْ), i.e. had We willed, We would have blinded them in this world as a punishment for disobeying Allah, Mighty and Majestic; but We have deferred their punishment to the Day of Resurrection. (فَاسْتَبَقُوا الصِّراطَ), i.e. then they would hasten along the road to their homes as soon as they were blinded, to reach their families.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: (وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَمَسَخْناهُمْ عَلى مَكانَتِهِمْ), i.e. had We willed, We would have transformed them in the place where they dared to disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (فَمَا اسْتَطاعُوا مُضِيًّا), i.e. and they would not be able to flee; (وَلا يَرْجِعُونَ) to their families. Al-Kisāʾī reported «طمس يطمِس ويطمُس». (وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَمَسَخْناهُمْ) «على مكانتهم»: one says «مكان» and «مكانة», «دار» and «دارة». Ibn al-Aʿrābī reported that the Arabs say, as the plural of «مكان», «أمكنة» and «مَكِنات», and that from it is the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "Leave the birds in their nests (makināt)." Abū Jaʿfar said: «مكِنات» is the plural of «مكِنة», and «مكِنة» and «مكان» have one meaning. People have spoken about the meaning of this ḥadīth. Some people said: do not startle them at night and do not hunt them; but al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it to Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna otherwise; he said: the Arabs used to scare birds from their nests when they wanted something done, taking good or bad omens from them, and the Prophet ﷺ forbade them that, saying "Leave the birds in their nests", i.e. do not scare them, for matters proceed according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed. Something other than this has been reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām in interpreting this verse; he interpreted it as concerning the Day of Resurrection. He said: when it is the Day of Resurrection and the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) is stretched out, a caller will call: "Let Muḥammad ﷺ and his community stand." They will stand, the righteous among them and the wicked, and follow him to cross the Bridge; and when they are upon it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will blot out the eyes of their wicked ones, and they will race for the Bridge — but how will they see it so as to cross it? Then he will call: "Let ʿĪsā ﷺ and his community stand," and they will stand, the righteous among them and the wicked, and their way will be that same way; and likewise all the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: (وَمَنْ نُعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ فِي الْخَلْقِ): Abū Isḥāq said: He replaces strength with weakness and youth with decrepitude. ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (نُنَكِّسْهُ) [with shadda] for intensity, and the light form [«نَنْكُسْه»] applies to little and much with one meaning.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
(وَما عَلَّمْناهُ الشِّعْرَ): it is authentically reported from him ﷺ that he said: [al-Rajaz] 364-
أنا النّبيّ لا كذب ... أنا ابن عبد المطّلب
(I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.)
The scholars have spoken about this. Some of them said: the narration is only with case endings, and if it is with case endings it is not poetry, because if he gave fatḥa or ḍamma or tanwīn to the bāʾ of the first line, and kasra to the bāʾ of the second line, it would depart from the metre of poetry. Some of them said: this metre is not poetry. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a denial of the obvious, because al-Khalīl and others have related poems of the Arabs in this [metre]. Among the good things said about this is the statement of Abū Isḥāq that the meaning of (وَما عَلَّمْناهُ الشِّعْرَ) is "We did not teach him to compose poetry", i.e. We did not make him a poet; and this does not prevent him from reciting some poetry. It has also been said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only informed that He did not teach him poetry, and did not inform that he does not recite poetry; and this is the apparent sense of the statement. A clear view has also been stated about it, whose holder claimed it is the consensus of the lexicographers: they said that whoever says a metrical utterance without intending poetry by it — it is not poetry; it merely coincides with poetry. And this is a clear view. (وَما يَنْبَغِي لَهُ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. nor is it made easy for him; and its interpretation is in the sense that composing poetry is not made easy for him, not reciting it. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ), i.e. what We have sent down to you is nothing but (ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ).

nahhas-irab:70-70.t:
﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ (70)

«لتنذر من كان حيّا…» [with tāʾ] is the reading of the people of Medina, and Abū ʿUbayd inclined to it. He said: the witness for it is «إنّما أنت منذر» ("You are only a warner"). The reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa is (لِيُنْذِرَ) [with yāʾ], whose meaning may be "that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may warn", or "that the Qurʾān may warn", or "that Muḥammad ﷺ may warn". Muḥammad ibn al-Samayfaʿ al-Yamānī read (لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كانَ حَيًّا). [Translator's note: the source prints Ibn al-Samayfaʿ's reading with the same vowelling as the standard one; his variant is not specified further.] Juwaybir reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: «من كان حيّا», i.e. whoever is a believer — because the believer is like the living in his accepting what benefits him. (وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ), i.e. it becomes due against them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will punish them; and this only becomes due against them after their disbelief. Some grammarians reported «لتَنْذَرَ من كان حيّا», i.e. "that you may know", from their saying «نذرتُ بالقوم أنذَر» when I learned about them and prepared for them. [Translator's note: the source prints this variant without vowels; the vowelling follows the derivation given.] And it was reported: «ويحقّ القول على الكافرين» in the sense of "the proof is made binding against them".

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: If you make «ما» in the sense of «الذي» (that which), the hāʾ is omitted because of the length of the noun; and if you make «ما» maṣdarī, there is no need to imply the hāʾ. The singular of «الأنعام» is «نَعَم», and «النَّعَم» is masculine.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
(فَمِنْها رَكُوبُهُمْ): Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reported from his father from ʿĀʾisha that she read «فمنها رَكوبتُهم». Abū Jaʿfar said: the Kufan grammarians reported that the Arabs say «امرأة صبور» and «شكور» without hāʾ, and they say «شاة حلوبة» and «ناقة ركوبة», because they wanted to distinguish between what performs the action and what the action falls on; so they dropped the hāʾ from what is an agent and kept it in what is an object, as ʿAntara said: [al-Kāmil] 365-
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأسحم
(Among them are forty-two milch-camels, black as the hidden wing-feathers of the jet-black raven.)
So on this basis it must be «ركوبتهم». As for the people of Basra, they say: the hāʾ was dropped by way of attribution (nasab). The proof for the first view is what al-Jarmī reported from Abū ʿUbayda; he said: «الرَّكوبة» is for one and for a group, and «الرَّكوب» is only for a group; so on this basis it is according to the masculine form of the plural. Abū Ḥātim claimed that «فمنها رُكوبهم» with ḍamma on the rāʾ is not permissible, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), whereas «الرَّكوب» is what is ridden. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «فمنها رُكوبهم» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, as you say «فمنها أكلُهم، ومنها شربُهم» ("from them is their eating, and from them their drinking").

nahhas-irab:73-73.t:
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ وَمَشارِبُ أَفَلا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ (73)

(وَلَهُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ وَمَشارِبُ): they are diptotes, because they are among the plurals which have no counterpart among singulars and are not themselves pluralized.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: This is the eloquent usage; some Arabs bring in «أن» and say «لعلّه أن يُنصَر».

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَهُمْ): meaning the [false] gods; they are given the plural of rational beings because He spoke of them with what is said of them. (وَهُمْ), meaning the disbelievers, (لَهُمْ), [for] the gods, (جُنْدٌ مُحْضَرُونَ). Al-Ḥasan said: they defend them and ward off from them. Qatāda said: they become angry on their behalf.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: (فَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ): this is the eloquent usage; some Arabs say «يُحْزِنْك». (إِنَّا) has kasra on the hamza where it comes after «القول», because it is resumptive.

nahhas-irab:78-79.t: (قالَ مَنْ يُحْيِ الْعِظامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ): the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, and assimilation is not permissible, lest two quiescent letters meet; and likewise (قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا الَّذِي أَنْشَأَها أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ).

nahhas-irab:80-81.t:
(الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ ناراً): «الشجر» is treated as masculine; and some Arabs say «الشجر الخضراء» [feminine], as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ) [al-Wāqiʿa: 52, 53].
It is reported that Sallām Abū al-Mundhir read (أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ بَلى). [Translator's note: the source prints Sallām's reading with the standard wording; the known variant attributed to him is «يقدر» in place of «بقادر».] I.e. the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than their creation, so the One who created the heavens and the earth is able to resurrect them.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t:
﴿إِنَّما أَمْرُهُ إِذا أَرادَ شَيْئاً أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ (82)

Al-Kisāʾī read «إنّما أمره إذا أراد شيئاً أن يقول له كن فيكونَ» in the accusative, conjoined to «يقول».

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: (مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ) — the keys of everything. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مَلَكوتى» and «مَلَكوت» in the speech of the Arabs mean «مُلْك» (dominion). The Arabs say: «جبروتى خيرٌ من رحموتى» ("being feared is better than being pitied").
